profile.overview: Finland has a single-structure basic education (perusopetus, grades 1-9) followed by general (lukio) or vocational upper secondary education. Since 1 August 2021 compulsory education lasts until age 18 or completion of an upper secondary qualification. Education is free from pre-primary to upper secondary; early childhood education and care carries income-related fees. Finnish and Swedish are the main languages of instruction, with Sámi used in the Sámi homeland. Non-state schools are few (about 3% of basic-level enrolments) and are publicly funded. The school year starts in August and ends on the last weekday of week 22 (late May or early June).
profile.compulsory_notes: Pre-primary education is mandatory in the year before basic education (usually the year the child turns 6). Compulsory education proper starts in the year the child turns 7 and ends at 18 or on completing an upper secondary qualification. Finland has compulsory education, not compulsory school attendance: home education is permitted.

instruction_languages.notes: Sámi languages are used as a language of instruction in some schools in the Sámi-speaking areas.
General upper secondary education in English offered from August 2026.

education_stages.name: Early childhood education and care
education_stages.notes: Optional. Municipal fees depend on family income, family size and hours of attendance.

education_stages.name: Pre-primary education
education_stages.notes: Mandatory since August 2015 in the year before basic education. About four hours a day.

education_stages.name: Basic education
education_stages.notes: Single structure covering primary (grades 1-6) and lower secondary (grades 7-9). Textbooks and materials are free.

education_stages.name: General upper secondary education
education_stages.notes: Typically three years, ending with the matriculation examination. Compulsory until 18 since August 2021.

education_stages.name: Vocational upper secondary education
education_stages.notes: Leads to a vocational upper secondary qualification. Compulsory until 18 since August 2021.

education_stages.name: Universities of applied sciences
education_stages.notes: Free for EU/EEA students; non-EU/EEA students pay fees for most English-taught programmes (since 2017).

education_stages.name: Universities
education_stages.notes: Bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees. Doctoral programmes are free for all; non-EU/EEA fees apply to most English-taught bachelor's and master's programmes.

country_curricula.notes: Set nationally; municipalities and schools draw up local curricula from it.
IB programmes are offered by both municipal upper secondary schools and international schools.

school_types.description: Most schools are maintained by municipalities or joint municipal authorities.
Privately run schools operating under a government licence and funded on the same per-pupil basis as municipal schools. About 3% of basic-level enrolments.
school_types.legal_status_notes: Need a government licence; may not charge tuition fees for basic education or operate for profit. Moderate fees are allowed only in specific cases (e.g. education abroad or in another language).

school_types.description: Steiner/Waldorf schools and kindergartens are private institutions, partly co-financed by the state when they meet national requirements.
Includes fee-paying international schools (e.g. International School of Helsinki: IB PYP, MYP, DP) and IB Diploma lines in municipal upper secondary schools.
Permitted because Finland requires education, not school attendance. Rare in practice.
school_types.legal_status_notes: No permit needed: guardians notify the municipality of residence, which monitors progress through an assigned teacher against curriculum goals.

school_types.description: Early childhood education and care. Municipal fees depend on family income, family size and weekly hours.
Research universities awarding bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees.
school_types.legal_status_notes: Tuition free for EU/EEA students; non-EU/EEA students pay fees for most English-taught programmes since 2017.
